MEEP geometry & field amplitudes — compact silica MZI mesh

All 2D Ez FDTD, MEEP 1.29, complex fields (|Ez| = envelope). Node/score scenes at the quantitative resolution (25 px/μm); the full mesh scene is a res-20 visual run (numbers in the report come from the res-25 node calibrations). Fields shown as |Ez| with sqrt/0.4 gamma so the weak arms stay visible.

1 · Compact node — geometry

52.6 μm node: 1.5 in · 8 s-bend · 5.8 coupler · 8 · 6 trim stub · 8 · 5.8 · 8 · 1.5 out, port pitch 4 μm, coupler gap 0.30 μm, w = 0.991 μm suspended silica in air.

2 · Compact node — CW steady-state |Ez|

Top: as-drawn (θ=0) the node is in its CROSS state — input on the upper guide exits the lower. Bottom: adding 0.30 μm of optical path on the trim stub (the GEOMETRIC θ=π/2 weight used by the fixed-weight mesh) splits the output 50/50 — this is the measured s = −0.04 point from the calibration.

3 · Score head — geometry

One calibrated 50/50 coupler. Arm A carries the token train delayed by one slot; arm B carries the undelayed train with a quarter-wave static offset.

4 · Score head — pulse trains interfering, |Ez| frames

Each frame: token pulses of the two trains meet PAIRWISE in the coupler (150 fs slots, scale model). The interference splits asymmetrically depending on the product s_t·s_{t−1} — the balanced detector difference per slot is the attention score. This is the run that reproduced the products to 1e-4.

5 · Full compact 5×5 Clements mesh — geometry

All 10 nodes in one FDTD cell: 5 columns × 52.6 μm, 5 guides at 4 μm pitch (275 × 17 μm active). Even columns pair rows (0,1),(2,3); odd columns pair (1,2),(3,4) — the Clements rectangle.

6 · Full mesh — pulse train cascading, |Ez| frames

A 3-token train (0.9, −0.7, 0.8) enters the middle port and cascades through the five columns; as-drawn nodes sit at their cross state, so power ping-pongs across the array — every coupler event in this picture is one MAC of the systolic convolution.
